subject: Performance SLO + Regional Routing Follow-up (Finova)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO + Regional Routing Follow-up (Finova)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to run through Finova's expected traffic patterns and the regional constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: user-facing chat assistant for account support and onboarding.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end < 300ms for chat (streaming enabled) in US/EU, target p95 < 500ms for APAC (initial).
- Throughput: steady-state 500 requests/sec, burst up to 2k RPS for promotional events.
- Concurrency: average 20 concurrent requests per region, but per-model concurrency could spike to ~200 during bursts.
- Streaming: yes — token-level streaming for assistant responses is required for better UX.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region; some APAC customers require data residency in APAC region.

Questions we raised
1) Do you expect the 500 RPS steady-state to be evenly split across regions or concentrated in the US with smaller EU/APAC tails?
2) Any hard constraints around cross-region fallback? (e.g., EU requests must never go to US infra)
3) Which endpoints/data are subject to EU/APAC residency (full request/response vs. logs/telemetry)?

Next steps (proposed)
- Aditya to run a quick capacity & cost sketch for the profile above (target: E2E p95s and cost per 1M tokens) — ETA EOD tomorrow.
- Rishi to propose a test plan for simulated bursts and streaming validation — ETA early next week.
- Marissa to share our SLO playbook and SOC2 excerpts (attached) and draft a mutual action plan for procurement.

Attachments: redwood_slo_playbook.pdf, SOC2-exhibit.zip

If that matches what you expect, we'll follow-up with the capacity sketch and a short test-run proposal.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Priya Sharma <priya@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@finova.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Regional Routing Follow-up (Finova)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That aligns closely with our expectations. A few clarifications: 

1) Regional distribution: current traffic is roughly 65% US, 25% EU, 10% APAC but marketing campaigns can make the APAC share spike over short windows.
2) Residency: EU production traffic (request/response and primary user data) must remain in EU for GDPR compliance. Logs/telemetry can be aggregated to US under our contract, but raw request/response payloads must not cross regions. APAC customers have a similar requirement for a subset of tenant data (we'll provide a list of tenant IDs).
3) Fallbacks: we need the option to failover across regions for high availability (e.g., EU->US) but only after explicit approval from our security/compliance team and with masking of any EU-only data. For now treat cross-region fallback as allowed only for stateless/anon requests.

Also: can you confirm whether streaming will maintain per-token latency guarantees (i.e., low first-byte latency) in Dedicated vs Hosted modes? We're evaluating both hosted and reserved capacity.

I'll loop in our security lead if needed after seeing your SOC2 excerpts.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Head of Platform
Finova
priya@finova.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Regional Routing Follow-up (Finova)

Hi Priya — quick technical notes in response to your questions: 

1) Streaming latency: for hosted (multi-tenant) we can typically hit first-byte latencies of ~60-120ms p95 for short prompts in US/EU on our verified models. Dedicated (reserved capacity) reduces p95 to ~40-80ms due to isolated pools and optimized kernel selection. Those numbers assume continuous KV caching and warm model instances.

2) Capacity sketch (initial):
- Steady 500 RPS global: request mix matters (chat generation vs embeddings). Assuming 60% chat generation, 40% light ops, estimated GPU vCore-equivalent: 6-8 dedicated GPUs for steady state with autoscale to handle 2k RPS bursts (burst policy uses warm spare capacity / fast scale-up).
- Concurrency planning: allow headroom for 3-4x observed concurrency spikes; propose default per-region concurrency limit of 300 for bursts.

3) Regional routing + residency: 
- We support routing by origin IP + tenant tag; can pin EU tenant IDs to EU-only pools.
- Cross-region fallback: can be implemented as a configurable policy at the tenant level with data filtering. We'll surface recommended defaults in the MAP.

I'll put together a short cost and SLO sketch (numbers + assumptions) and share this afternoon. Rishi, want to add the proposed test harness items?

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@finova.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Regional Routing Follow-up (Finova)

Thanks — adding detail from a validation / testing perspective: 

Proposed test plan (high level)
1) Baseline latency + streaming test (per-region)
   - Run synthetic steady-state (500 RPS profile) in US/EU/APAC with representative prompt distribution. Measure first-byte and token-stream p50/p95/p99.
2) Burst scaling test
   - Ramp from 500 -> 2k RPS over 5 minutes, hold 2k for 10 minutes, then ramp down. Validate tail latency and error rates.
3) Concurrency spike test
   - Simulate 200 concurrent long-running sessions (multi-turn chat) and validate KV cache reuse and memory footprint.
4) Residency/fallback test cases
   - Validate EU-tenant pinned routing (no data leaves EU).
   - Simulate EU->US fallback for allowed anon requests and verify masking and audit logs.

Test harness & metrics we will produce- Per-region p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and per-token latencies
- CPU/GPU utilization, memory, and stalls during bursts
- End-to-end availability and error rates by tenant
- Audit log snapshots to demonstrate residency behavior

I can run an initial dry-run in our staging regions next week and share the artifacts (JMeter scripts, k6 config, Grafana dashboards). Would Finova want the raw test results or only summarized reports for security/compliance?

Rishi
Sr. Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Regional Routing Follow-up (Finova)

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick responses. Priya, appreciate the distribution detail and the residency clarity; that helps us pin the MAP items. To summarize agreed actions and timelines:

- Aditya: capacity + cost sketch and assumptions (EOD today).
- Rishi: staging test harness dry-run and draft k6/JMeter configs (ETA Tue 2026-10-20).
- Marissa: send a short MAP with milestones (POC -> procurement -> Dedicated reserve discussion) and include the SOC2 excerpts + SLO playbook (sent).
- Priya: share the tenant ID list for APAC residency and confirm whether logs/telemetry can be aggregated outside region (if okay we'll mark as allowed).

We'll also include a short demo of streaming performance on the next call if you'd like — happy to set up a 30-minute session mid-next-week. Let me know what times work for you.

Best,
